outcomeNote: A bare mishna ruling with no dialectic and no named disputants; the contrast with ערכין is a rubric, not a dispute between parties.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ ״דָּמֵי יְדֵי עָלַי״ — שָׁמִין אוֹתוֹ כַּמָּה הוּא שָׁוָה בַּיָּד וּבְלֹא יָד. זֶה חוֹמֶר בַּנְּדָרִים מִבַּעֲרָכִין.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If one vows: It is incumbent «upon me» to donate the «assessment of my forearm,» the court «appraises him» to determine «how much he is worth with a forearm and» how much he is worth «without a forearm,» and he pays the difference. «This is» a halakha that is more «stringent with regard to vows» of assessment «than with regard to valuations,» as one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my forearm, is exempt from paying.

moves.summary: the mishna rules that one who vows the assessment of his forearm is appraised with and without it and pays the difference
the mishna labels this ruling a stringency of vows of assessment over valuations
